scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The folk dances of the Sourashtra people originate within the ethno-linguistic Hindu Sourashtra community of South India.
These performance traditions have developed as integral parts of religious celebrations and social gatherings.

The Gebbi dance traces its symbolic identity to the concept of shakti (cosmic energy) and derives its name from Garba-graha, linking its origin to temple sanctuary worship where an illuminated clay pot or water-filled vessel serves as a temporary dwelling for deities.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Gebbi is performed by women on various religious occasions as a worship of shakti, the primordial cosmic energy, symbolic of divine creation and cosmic order.
The water-filled pot represents the outer world and acts as a sacred vessel where deities are invited to reside for blessings.
Dandi natana is performed as a social and ritual stick dance during festive gatherings.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The Gebbi is performed by women in counterclockwise circular formations around a sacred central point, such as a lamp (Thandili Diva) or an image of a mother goddess.
If space is limited or many participants join, dancers form concentric circles moving in opposite directions.
The dance incorporates circular and spiral paths with handclaps, starting slowly and gradually increasing in speed.
Watch for Gebbi Circle, Dandi Strike, Konangi Jesters Mime.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears

Formation: Counterclockwise circles around a central lamp or vessel; concentric circles moving in opposite directions when space is constrained; expanding paired formations multiplying from 2 to 4, 8, 16 performers.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Listen for the Sticks (Dandi), Human voice (Devotional bhakti singing).

The sonic environment is characterized by vocal devotional (bhakti) songs sung in chorus, punctuated by synchronized handclaps in Gebbi or the sharp percussive clatter of wood striking wood in Dandi natana.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The folk dances of Sourashtra are categorized as subclasses of Indian folk dance, preserved specifically within the Sourashtra ethno-linguistic community of South India.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Sourashtra folk dance is variant of Garba: Gebbi shares etymological and ritual roots (Garba-graha, worshipping Shakti around a central vessel) with Garba.
Sourashtra folk dance is sibling of Kolattam: Dandi natana shares stick dance mechanics (kolane) with South Indian Kolattam traditions.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Gebbi is a sacred devotional dance symbolising shakti and involves inviting deities to temporarily reside within a water vessel or illuminated lamp; sacred spaces and altars should be treated with traditional Hindu reverence.

visual_brief.setting_notes: Gebbi is performed by women on various religious occasions as a worship of shakti, the primordial cosmic energy, symbolic of divine creation and cosmic order. The water-filled pot represents the outer world and acts as a sacred vessel where deities are invited to reside for blessings. Dandi natana is performed as a social and ritual stick dance during festive gatherings. The Konangi is presented during the Rama Navami festival by male performers to convey moral values and preach good thoughts to society through comical narrative theatre.
